name.evidence: We introduce XTREME-S , a new benchmark to evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations in many languages.

description.evidence: We introduce XTREME-S , a new benchmark to evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations in many languages. XTREME-S covers four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation and retrieval.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We collect between one and three recordings for each sentence ( 2:3on average), and build new train-dev-test splits...

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Fleurs is the speech version of the FLoRes machine translation benchmark [ 38]. We use 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest publicly available sets...

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: FLEURS is a dataset that is complete at more than 97%. Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings).

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Fleurs is the speech version of the FLoRes machine translation benchmark [ 38]. We use 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest publicly available sets, in 102 languages.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We build new train-dev-test splits with 1509 ,150and350sentences for train, dev and test respectively.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: We collect between one and three recordings for each sentence ( 2:3on average)...

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings). Updates will be made on our platform.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Making speech technology available in all languages is especially important to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Intemet, and the possibility to make their content and culture known outside of their language cluster.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: We observe in Table 4 that results are much better on the Westem European group (with 11.5 average WER) than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African (26.7 average WER) or South Asian (20.7), which can be explained in part due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in WE languages from MLS and V oxPopuli.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: In general, speech classification tasks are prone to overfitting given the discrepancy between the richness of the input signal (speaker, domain, recording conditions) and the small number of output labels.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: XTREME-S covers four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation and retrieval.
